correctness.rationale: Reconstructed polarization Q(s+d)=Q(s-d)=4 and B(s,d)=0 on norm-one conic: for s!=0 the prescribed difference d has at most two opposite solutions, including isotropic s where Q(d)=0 contradicts 4. Character orthogonality gives exact T(f)=2S²-Σw_u²+8ReΣ_{i<j}z_i conjugate(z_j); p<=1 yields 2-1/m and arbitrary phases. For p>=2, AM-GM and pair mass Cauchy yield T≤2S²+(1-3/(2p))P²-R²/(m-2p), with maximum only at P=S: unpaired points vanish, all intact pairs equal amplitudes and aligned products. Counting split/nonsplit norm-one groups gives h=(q-1)/2 or (q+1)/2 and feasible p range max(0,m-h)..floor(m/2). Independently enumerated ALL 396 nonempty masks in split and nonsplit q=5,7 cases and confirmed all extremal witnesses by direct convolution. This finite check corroborates but does not replace proof for all odd prime powers.

originality.rationale: The complete arbitrary-mask, split/nonsplit conic spectrum and two-intact-pair extremizer transition is stronger than the earlier specific whole-conic and one-deletion claims. Direct reading of the published one-deletion primary theorem shows q=3 gives p=1, m=3, 5/3; q>=5 gives p=(q-1)/2, m=q, 3-3/(q-1), all exact consequences here, not conversely. Full-text 2405.16647 examines paraboloids, a hyperbolic paraboloid and higher-dimensional cones, not all planar masked norm-one conics. Residual risk remains an unpublished/general uniquely-represented-nonzero-two-sums optimization.
residual_risks: An older unindexed general sharp Λ(4) optimization for all finite sets with unique nonzero unordered two sums could imply some or all of the formula; not excluded by finite search.
